profile: The pinned SQLite 3.47.2 ordinary base-table DELETE profile in sqlite-delete-v1.json.
scope: An ordinary DELETE can return an ordered list of named columns from its resolved pre-delete row. Analyze admits unqualified column references and unqualified star expansion.

returned-column.role: One output position in the RETURNING layout of a single-target DELETE
returned-column.structure: A readonly ColumnReference at target occurrence zero and a readonly decoded output name.
returned-column.conditions: The returned column has occurrence zero. The owning DELETE verifies slot membership, copies the ordered list and bounds it to 2000 fields.
returned-column.meaning: Read the referenced value of the row before removal and attach the recorded output label.
returned-column.externalInterpretation: Resolve the same absolute ordinary table and column layout at evaluation. The table's triggers and foreign keys participate in the deletion.
returned-column.sql: Render the target slot as an unqualified quoted column in RETURNING and emit its quoted output label.

observations: Ordered result labels, exact SQLite storage classes, NULL, duplicate rows and predicate parameter registration
